corrected_verdict: KNOWN. lem:avg is a trivial specialisation of Morwani et al. (ICLR 2024) Sec 3.2: g' >= g for any class weighting tau, averaged under uniform q, with tau set to the point mass on y-delta. Mathematically it is just "min <= any convex combination", i.e. the max-min / weak-duality inequality (Boyd and Vandenberghe Sec 5.4.1, eq. 5.46). Keeping one inequality per delta instead of Morwani's uniform tau helps the exposition (it sets up the later min over offsets) but is not a result. Credit is also owed to Li et al. (AISTATS 2025), who define the n-input single-neuron eta (Def. D.5) and restate the class-weighted margin for k inputs (Def. 3.6). No prior paper states the network-level per-delta form, but Morwani's general-tau framework already covers it.
issues:
I fetched and checked each of the checker's claims myself (arXiv abs page, arXiv v2 HTML full text, OpenReview API note i9wDX850jR "ICLR 2024 spotlight"). All of them hold:
- Sec 3.2 contains "Note that g'(theta,x,y) >= g(theta,x,y) as g' replaces the max by a weighted sum."
- The Sec 3 preamble writes gamma* = max_theta min_q E_q g.
- Sec 3.3 step 1 takes q* uniform.
- App. F.1 defines eta_{u,v,w}(delta) := E_{a,b}[(u(a)+v(b))^2 w(a+b-delta)] and maximises Eq. (4). The uniform tau = 1/(p-1) is stated in the Sec 4 proof outline of Thm 7 and used in F.1.
- The bib entry is correct.

Missed by the checker:
(1) Li, Liang, Shi, Song, Zhou (arXiv:2402.09469v4, "AIStats 2025") already have the n-operand version of the eta the paper generalises, and they restate the class-weighted margin (Def. 3.6). Their Def. D.5 (App. D.4) is eta_{u_1..u_k,w}(delta) := E[(u_1(a_1)+...+u_k(a_k))^k w(a_1+...+a_k-delta)], with uniform tau (Lemma D.7). The key li2025nsum is in refs.bib but is cited in no current section; intro.tex l.22 has only a TODO. The paper should credit it at approach.tex l.11, e.g. "\citet[Appendix~F.1]{morwani2024feature} (for n operands, \citealp[Definition~D.5]{li2025nsum})".
(2) The sentence "interference averages away" is the network-level form of Morwani App. F.1's step "E_{a,b}[u(a)^2 w(a+b-delta)] = 0". An optional "as in Morwani App. F.1" would credit it.
(3) Relevant to R2, not R1: Morwani App. F.3 already uses the multidimensional DFT diagonal f^(j,j,-j), which is the paper's beta_j. The Fourier expansion of eta is also the textbook identity for averages over solutions of a linear equation (Zhao 2023, Ch. 6, Prop. 6.1.9 and Ex. 6.1.11).

Both of the checker's pointer fixes (Section 3.2, Appendix F.1) are correct but optional, since "Section 3" is already accurate. The numbering comes from arXiv v2 (19 Feb 2024). I could not compare it with the OpenReview camera-ready PDF, which sits behind a browser check.

Search coverage: I checked Mohamadi et al. 2407.12332 and 2511.23443 and found no averaged or per-delta margin bound. WebSearch hit its session cap and Semantic Scholar returned 429, so I used the arXiv API, OpenAlex and OpenReview instead. I did not reach MathOverflow, but the fact is elementary.

extra_citations.why: Already in refs.bib but not cited in any current section. Def. D.5 (App. D.4) defines the k-input single-neuron eta_{u_1..u_k,w}(delta), and Def. 3.6 restates the class-weighted margin for k inputs. Our n-operand eta_theta is the network-level version of their eta, so they should be credited at approach.tex l.11 next to Morwani App. F.1.

Optional, and for eq:spectrum / app:spectrum rather than lem:avg. For a product neuron, eta(delta) is a shifted average over solutions of a linear equation. Its Fourier expansion is the textbook identity in Ch. 6 (Prop. 6.1.9 'Fourier and 3-AP'; Exercise 6.1.11 gives the general k-variable form sum_r prod f^_i(a_i r)). Cite at chapter level, because the manuscript's pagination differs from the published book.

Optional, low priority. Sec 5.4.1, eq. (5.46) is the max-min inequality sup_z inf_w f <= inf_w sup_z f 'for any f'. This is the classical fact behind 'min margin <= any averaged class-weighted margin', and Morwani cite it for their Lemma 2. Only needed if the paper frames lem:avg as weak duality.
